title: Four hash-addressed logical experts over shared HashedNet buckets
dataset: scikit-learn load_digits, fixed 8x8 grayscale digit features and labels
task_construction: Four expert roles use class group = digit_label mod 4; each expert is trained only on its group's examples and emits logits only for classes in that group. A supervised shared linear router predicts the group from the 64 input features. End-to-end quality uses router-selected top-1 expert; oracle-expert quality is reported separately.
model: Four logical 64->128 ReLU->10 experts plus a shared 64->4 router; compression is restricted to expert first-layer matrices unless the method explicitly uses independent dense experts.
hypothesis: One shared 2,048-bucket physical table plus small per-expert Mirror input Views can provide four useful logical expert functions at much lower actual bytes than independent hashed/dense experts, while improving quality over ordinary tied experts and native salted shared hashing.
physical_object: Shared 2,048-value hash bucket vector, shared output projection, and router; independent experts have separate tables/weights
mirror_coordinate: Thirty-two learned adjacent-pair Givens angles per expert, applied before the same shared hashed FFN
methods: independent 2,048-bucket expert tables with shared output projection
shared hash table with expert-specific native hash salts
shared hash table with expert-specific learned Givens Views (Mirror)
shared hash table with expert-specific diagonal input gates
shared hash table with expert-specific rank-one residuals

hashing.mapping: Uniform bucket and independent +/-1 sign from NumPy PCG64. Shared-map methods use one deterministic map; salted and independent-table methods use deterministic expert-specific map seeds regenerated from paid 32-bit seeds.

training.router_loss: Cross entropy to y mod 4 on each full minibatch
training.expert_loss: Sum of cross entropy for each expert on minibatch examples assigned to that expert; other classes masked from that expert's logits
training.initialization: Same frozen initialization code for all methods; expert-specific Givens start at zero, gates at one, rank-one factors at Gaussian std 0.01

development.selection: No hyperparameter grid. Architecture, bucket count, training schedule and gates frozen before training.

fresh.data_splits: Independent stratified splits of the same fixed load_digits corpus
fresh.open_rule: Run fresh splits only if both dev seeds satisfy the complete Mirror quality, byte and expert-usefulness gate.

storage.authority: actual uncompressed NPZ inference payload bytes after load/serialize roundtrip
paid_objects: all physical hash tables or dense expert tensors
storage.deterministic_reconstruction: Bucket indices/signs are regenerated from paid seeds and committed deterministic hash code; seed, method code, and schema are paid metadata.

report: number of experts executed at inference
serialized inference wall time/examples per second

primary_metrics: router-selected top-1 accuracy and cross entropy
success_gate: Both dev seeds: Mirror top-1 accuracy is >=+1.0 percentage point over ordinary tied hash and salted shared-hash controls, within 2.0 points of independent dense experts, all four oracle experts have >=0.80 conditional accuracy and router uses each expert on >=10% of examples, Mirror bytes <=1.05x salted shared hash bytes, and no diagonal/rank-one control matches or beats Mirror within 1.0 point at <=1.10x Mirror bytes.
failure_gate: Any quality/byte/usefulness gate miss or byte-near simple control matching Mirror is FAIL for the Mirror claim; fresh remains sealed.
boundaries: Four class-group experts over one small image task are not broad MoE capacity evidence
Expert count is not independent capacity; conditional quality, routing, bytes, and compute decide usefulness
One shared-table vs salt/view screen is mechanism evidence only
Fixed-update training is not near-convergence capacity
Learned Givens must beat the native per-expert salt and simple gate/residual controls
